pattern:
This share holds 7 wrong runs: positions 0-6, sorted by run_dir. All are attribution failures that happened after complete discovery: every run traversed the full chain and displayed the full gold body, so there is no SEARCH_FAILURE or DISCOVERY_WITHOUT_INSPECTION. The runs fall into two groups.

(a) Five Claude runs on CHART-PIE-TREATMENT-03 (3 post-hardening, 2 pre-hardening):
- Rank 1 is the definer PlotUtilities::drift in 5/5.
- Gold ShapeUtilities::shift is ranked 6th in 4/5, below even the plumbing hops and the facade. It is 3rd only in the one run that read the javadocs and named shift as a co-candidate.
- In every run, ownership was settled by hand arithmetic on the test's expected value (87.5). That value fixes only the net sign. The agents then defaulted to a convention that a drift is exploded minus unexploded and that shift adds. In run-001 (post-hardening) the agent read that convention into drift's direction-neutral javadoc (LOCAL_ODDNESS_BIAS); the other four did not read any javadoc (CONVENTION_PRIOR).
- No run fetched the decisive distant evidence: the PiePlot draw/drawPie ring containment, the facade javadoc, or RingPlot.drawItem.
- 3/5 tried the allowed test, but defects4j failed on the missing String::Interpolate Perl module, so no actual failure value was ever observed. Runs were short (7-10 calls).

(b) Two GPT-5.6 Conversion treatment runs (branch dispatch run-004, indirect dispatch run-003):
- Both resolved the dispatch, read the facade's 'in bits' contract, and ran runtime probes (javap/Python, jshell).
- Both explicitly named overlay's (index + at) * width as the concrete defect, yet ranked the tested facade intArrayToLong first as the entry point and contract owner, with gold 2nd (ENTRY_POINT_BIAS).
- Both runs also appear in all_runs.json under diagnostic-noncanonical-v3, and their prompt workspace paths point there. Deduplicate before counting.

Common thread: in ownership-split chains (definer vs adapter, or contract owner vs arithmetic owner), the models localise the fault behaviourally but give rank 1 to a co-owner. Claude picks the producer whose arithmetic looks reversed; GPT-5.6 picks the tested contract owner.
